pr_title: Add resource for installing .pkg files on macOS
pr_body:
## Description
This PR adds a new resource: `macos_pkg`, adapted in part from `dmg_package`. It lets users install .pkg and .mpkg files on macOS nodes from either a local or remote source.

### Example usage

Install osquery from a remote source:

```ruby
macos_pkg 'osquery' do
  checksum   '1fea8ac9b603851d2e76c5fc73138a468a3075a3002c8cb1fd7fff53b889c4dd'
  package_id 'io.osquery.agent'
  source     'https://pkg.osquery.io/darwin/osquery-5.8.2.pkg'
  action     :install
end
```

Ditto, except it's a local file:
```ruby
macos_pkg 'Local file example' do
  checksum   '1fea8ac9b603851d2e76c5fc73138a468a3075a3002c8cb1fd7fff53b889c4dd'
  file       '/Users/foo/osquery-5.8.2.pkg'
  package_id 'io.osquery.agent'
  action     :install
end
```
The resources above will be skipped after the first run, since the `package_id` property is detected as installed.

This resource fails since it has no `source` or `file` property:

```ruby
macos_pkg 'incomplete resource definition' do
  checksum '28a23e9c51beae82d7b8ed412472abcce73623e7880e552856c6a3dcf475d48c'
  package_id 'io.osquery.agent'
end
```

## Related Issue
Closes #11398

issue_context.title: Expose pkg/app code inside of `dmg_package` as their own resources
issue_context.body:
### Describe the Enhancement:

Currently today you can only use the pkg/app installing code in chef if it's inside of a dimg, but more and more people are distributing straight pkg or app files. It would be useful to be able to have Chef install those, so we should expose that support as it's own resource.

### Describe the Need:

See above

### Current Alternative

`execute` rules

### Can We Help You Implement This?:

I don't know I"ll get around to it anytime soon, but it's probably a good task for someone trying to get familiar with the codebase.

review_comments: Ultimately, this should be using the `Chef::Resource::Package` pattern that other package providers use. (See [`lib/chef/resource/homebrew_package.rb`](https://github.com/chef/chef/blob/main/lib/chef/resource/homebrew_package.rb)).
macOS pkg files don't really have a concept of uninstalling. Would the `Chef::Resource::Package` pattern  still be useful when the only action in allowed_actions is :install?

You can override them and mark them unsupported.

But we should support uninstall along these lines: https://gist.github.com/githubutilities/b5318d08a4b970d104f1

List the files, remove them, and then do the `--forget`.
It seems odd to have an :install action that then tells people to run manual commands. We probably want an `:upgrade` action to do something sensible here.
Would adding an `:upgrade` action and implicitly forgetting the install receipt by running `pkgutil --forget` in the resource be an unexpected behavior for users?
If it will not leave cruft from the previous version, that's probably fine. Otherwise, I would uninstall as indicated above before doing the install.
